key_insight: Snoring audio alone can distinguish palatal from epiglottic upper-airway obstruction in OSA with strong machine-learning performance.
clinical_relevance: This points to a non-invasive way to help phenotype obstruction site and potentially complement sleep endoscopy when access is limited.
method: 159 DISE recordings from adults with moderate, non-positional OSA
Snoring events were blinded, anatomically labeled, and only consensus events were used
Spectral, cepstral, temporal, and harmonic features were selected and classified with SVM and MLP using patient-independent nested cross-validation
evidence_signal: The final dataset contained 1,759 snoring events, and both models reached ROC AUC 0.90 ± 0.03 with balanced accuracy around 0.81–0.83 under patient-independent validation.
watch_item: Results come from a retrospective, single-dataset study using only events with complete expert agreement, so external validation and real-world robustness are still needed.
paper_title: The sound of snoring: AI-based acoustic phenotyping of upper airway obstruction in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
